title: Chairman Mao Inspects  Shanghai Steel Factory
description: Jin Shangyi(1934- )was born in Jiaozuo, Henan Province. He is a doctorial supervisor in China Central Academy of Fine Arts, and the president of China Artists Association. This work was created by Jin Shangyi for Beijing metro station, which was under construction, in 1969. The theme is "Chairman Mao in the Steelworks". This painting is Jin's only oil painting in the subject of industry.

title: Chairman Mao, Premier Zhou and Leader Zhu
artist: Du Jian, Gao Yaguang, Su Gaoli
description: Du Jian(1933- )was born in Nanhai, Guangdong Province. He taught in Fine Arts School Affiliated to China Central Academy of Fine Arts and China Central Academy of Fine Arts. Gao Yaguang(1932-)was born in Tao'an, Jilin Province. He taught in Fine Arts School Affiliated to China Central Academy of Fine Arts. Su Gaoli(1937-)was born in Pingding County, Shanxi Province. He was the professor of China Central Academy of Fine Arts. Shortly after the Cultural Revolution, artistic creation of Chinese leaders became more realistic. This painting is a significance one showing this change.

title: Sentinel of Our Great Motherland
description: Shen Jiawei(1948- )was born in Shanghai. He is now lives and works in Australia. The historical background of this painting is the relation between China and Soviet Union at that time. Heilongjiang, as the border of China and Soviet Union, became the focus of China and abroad in the result of "Zhenbao Island Event" in March 1969.

title: In Front of Tian An Men
description: Sun Zixi(1929- )was born in Shandong. He entered China Central Academy of Fine Arts in 1955, and taught there after graduation. He engages in art education and art creation in long-term basis. The artist seleted the moment of people from all nationalities of China standing in front of Tian An Men waiting for the photographing, in a festival morning in the 1950s. This piece of work is a recreation during Cultural Revolution, the artist changed the letters in two banners on Tian An Men into traditional Chinese, in order to restore the feature of the time in the 1950s.

title: On the March
description: Tang Muli(1947- )was born in Shanghai. He obtained a master degree at Central Academy of Fine Arts in 1980, and another master degree at Royal College of Art in UK in 1984. This painting presents Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai and soldiers of the Eighth Route Army were advancing together in the magnificent mountains.

title: Chairman Mao Inspection of Countryside in Guangdong
description: Chen Yanning(1945-)was born in Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, and graduated from Guangzhou Academy of Fine Arts in 1965. This painting is based on Mao Zedong inspected Tangxia, where is the suburb of Guangzhou, in 1958. It describes Mao's support on new things of revolution, and his activity in Tangxia.

title: Ping'an Epistle in Cursive Script
description: Wang Xizhi (306-361), also known by his zi (designated name) Yi Shao, was born in Linyi. He is a Chinese calligrapher of the Eastern Jin dynasty, who is good at incorporating clerical script, cursive script, regular script and running script in his own style. He and his son were renowned as the “Two Wangs”. Nowadays, except from Wang Xizhi’s stele rubbing of calligraphy, other pieces were mostly calligraphy copy from Tang dynasty or ancient period. Calligraphy in this silk handscroll Pingantie, can be also called by Gaojiangdaotie. In this handscroll, he used delicate but vigorous brushstrokes to produce his unique leisurely style. Wang Xizhi’s cursive script presented an inspiring atmosphere.

title: Rare Birds Painted from Life
description: Zhao Ji (1082-1135), also known as Emperor Song Huizong, reigned over China from 1100 to 1125. During this period, he collected a large number of ancient artifacts, calligraphic works and paintings，recruited painters, expanded the School of Painting in the Hanlin Academy (hanlinyuan)，and asked his ministers to compile The Calligraphy Collection of the Xuanhe Period (xuanheshupu). and The Painting Collection of the Xuanhe Period (xuanhehuapu). Zhao Ji was highly accomplished in calligraphy and painting. His regular script, “Slender Gold Script” (Shoujinshu), as named by the Emperor himself, is based on Xue Yao's calligraphic style. Zhao emphasized the importance of sketching and was famous for the close resemblance of his meticulous paintings to the original real objects. He was equally good at painting flowers and birds, and, allegedly, used raw lacquer to paint the eyes of birds, which made them miraculously lifelike.

title: Pictures of Auspicious Omens
artist: Anonymous(Formerly attributed to Xiao Zhao),Song Dynasty
medium: Handscroll, Ink and colour on silk
description: There are several existing copies of the the “Illustrations of Auspicious Omens” (Ruiyingtu), the earliest of which was created in the Southern Song dynasty. Three scrolls of the painting were owned by a powerful minister called Yan Song, as were recorded in The Catalogue of the Handscroll Paintings Collected by the Yan Family (yanshihuapinshoujuanmu), in which the painter was identified as Xiao Zhao. Another scroll of the painting was recorded by Sun Feng in the Ming dynasty as the “Illustrations of Auspicious Omens” before the Coronation of Emperor Gaozong”(songgaozongruiyingtu). According to Sun Feng, “this painting was created by Li Song and inscribed by Cao Xun.” None of the extant copies of the Illustrations of Auspicious Omens” was signed. Thus, the so-called painter, either Xiao Zhao or Li Song, is merely a speculation made by later generations. The figures, their clothes and hats, the architectures and utensils are in accordance with the traditions in the Song Dynasty. The way the stones and trees were painted and the tracing of the figures create a forceful, refined, gentle, and majestic effect on this piece of colorful and densely woven silk. The men’s clothes, horse armor, curtains and screens of the houses, trees, stones, as well as mountain peaks and ranges were mainly painted in vermilion, while the overall color effect was well balanced by using such colors as purple, bluish gray, umber, and black. This way of coloring carries a typical feature seen in the early Southern Song dynasty, resembling that of “Lady Wenji’s Return to Han” (wenjiguihantu, the work was passed to Li Tang, and is now kept in the National Palace Museum in Taipei), “The Riverside Scene at the Qing Ming Festival” (qingmingshanghetu, kept in the Palace Museum in Beijing) by Zhang Zeduan, and “Women’s Filial Piety” (nvxiaojingtu, kept in the Palace Museum in Beijing).

title: Eighteen Luohans Scroll Handscroll
medium: Handscroll, Ink and colour on paper Dated 1615
description: Wu Bin, born in Putian, Fujian province, was also known by his zi (designated name) Wenzhong, and his hao (literary name) Zhiyin, Zhiyin’s antoutuo, and Zhianfaseng. He was a painter at the Emperor’s Palace (neiting) in the Wanli period, and the secretary of Gong Bu Ministry of Works. He excelled at landscape painting and was particularly good at figure painting. The Buddha images and human figures painted by Wu feature unique appearances and forms, enabling him to stand out from the earlier painters.

title: The Gathering at the Orchid Pavilion
medium: Handscroll, Ink and colour on silk Dated 1557
description: Wen Zhengming (1470-1599) had an original name called Wen Bi, and his zi (designated name) was Zhengming, which the painter mainly used to refer to himself. He later changed his zi to Zhengzhong. His hao (literary name) was Hengshanjushi. Born in Changzhou (today’s Wuxian, Jiangsu province, he was once a Compiling Assistant (daizhao) in the Hanlin Academy (hanlinyuan), but later he resigned and returned to his hometown. Wen was renowned as one of the “Four Talents in Wuzhong” together with Zhu Yunming, Tang yin, and Xu Zhenqing. As a calligrapher, he specialized in running script, cursive script, as well as clerical script. He also excelled at landscape painting and imitated the style in the Song and Yuan Dynasties. His use of ink and brush is forceful, smooth, graceful and refined. He was also good at painting flowers, orchids, bamboos, and figures. He was renowned as one of the “Four Master Painters of the Ming Dynasty” together with Shen Zhou, Tang Yin, and Qiu Ying.

title: Blue-and-White Porcelain Vase with Design of Ten Thousands Characters “Shou”
description: The vase has a square rim, a short neck, a tray-shaped mouth, and plump shoulders. Its body becomes slender below the shoulders, but the overall shape is steady. It has a sand base with no glaze. It is heavly potted with bright tone of blue-and-white. Outside of the vase is decorated with ten thousands“Shou”. Each“Shou”is different in terms of their scripts. Some are seal scripts while others are variant scripts. Their layout is dense and not messy, which fully demonstrates the beauty of seal calligraphy. The vase is an extremely rare blue-and-white vessel during the Kangxi period.

title: Cong Vase with Light Bluish-green Glaze
description: Cong-shaped vase with a square body, a round mouth, a short cylindrical neck and a ring foot. The sizes of the mouth and foot are similar. The vase has rectangular sizes with raised horizontal grooves. Cong vase imitates the shape of the Neolithic ritual-Cong Jade, and makes a few changes. Both Guan Kiln and Longquan Kiln have this type of vessel.

title: Yellow-ground Porcelain Openwork Revolving Vase with Design of Indian Lotus and Medallion Dragon in Famille Rose Enamel
medium: Qianlong Reign, Qing Dynasty Hight:38.1cm Qianlong Six-Character Seal Mark and of the Period
description: The vase has a flared mouth, a waisted neck and base, plump shoulders, cylindrical belly, and a raised ring-foot. The inner cylindrical body and the base are glazed with turquoise green. The craftsmanship of the revolving vase is very complicated, which involves openwork, revolving and emblishment. The neck is joined to the interior of the vase. The axis of the vase which connects the reticulated exterior, the base and the foot altogether can spin. Inside of the vase is decorated with twelve magpies, turquoise, Buddha’s hand, and Ganoderma, with the meaning of longevity and good fortune. The components of the revolving vase can not be deformed during the firing and the shrinkage ratio must be similar. This demonstrates the superb craftsmanship and achievements of the imperial kiln porcelain during the Qianlong period.

title: Cup Decorated with Fowls in Doucai Enamel
medium: Chenhua Reign，Ming Dynasty Mouth Diameter: 8.2cm Chenhua Six-Character Mark and of the Period
description: The “Chicken Cup” is wide at the top and narrow at the bottom, with a slanted wall, an open mouth, and a concave foot. The texture is fine and glossy. The glaze is gentle and lustrous. Outside painted with two separate scenes of cockerel and hen with five chicks in a landscape in underglaze blue outlines and overglaze iron red, yellow, and green enamels. Because of those vivid scenes and the elegant composition, there are many imitations in later generations.

title: An Exceptionally Large, Blue-and-White Lobed “Fish Pond” Bowl
medium: Xuande Reign, Ming Dynasty Mouth Diameter: 23cm Xuande Six-Character Mark and of the Period
description: The deep porcelain bowl has a flared mouth and a low foot ring. It is exquisitely painted in rich underglaze blue-and-white with dark brown spots in some areas. The glaze is very lustrous, and its texture is fine and glossy. The body of the bowl has ten edges. The outside of the bowl is decorated with lotus pond, algae, and four swimming fishes. Inside is decorated with a double blue line edging the rim, lotus flowers, algae, and two swimming fishes. Although the Xuande bowls with similar fish algae blue-and-white patterns are handed down from generations to generations, only two bowls from the Taipei National Palace Museum can be compared with this one. However, those two bowls are smaller than this one. This porcelain bowl is unrivalled in terms of sizes, patterns, painting techniques, and shapes.

title: Twelve Blue-and-White “Month” Cups
medium: Kangxi Reign, Qing Dynasty Mouth Diameter:6.6cm Kangxi Six-Character Mark and of the Period
description: The cups have flared mouths, ring feet, and are thinly potted, with a shinny glaze, delicate outlines, and rich layers. Each cup is decorated with a different floral design representing the twelve months of the lunar calendar, complemented by a different poem with relevance to the particular flower depicted, ending with the seal reading shang (appreciation).The combination of painting, poem and seal on a porcelain surfaces is very literary. Due to the difference in climate between the north and the south, the flowers circulating in different places are different. The flowers on this set of twelve cups are common in the north, and the poems inscribed are all couplets from Tang Dynasty Poems. There are many copies of “Month” cups from the Yongzheng to the Republic of China. Some are blue-and-white, others are coloured.

title: Red Sandalwood Throne Carved with Auspicious Bats, Clouds, and Dragons
description: The throne is meticulously carved from the finest and precious red sandalwood. The texture is exquisite and intense, with a simple and unsophisticated luster. The design of ripple and dragons among clouds is solemn and magestic. The dragons are lifelike and are the products of fine craftsmanship. Such superb sculptural technique - relief comes from the skilled craftsmen in the Qung Palace Manufacturing Office. The throne is huge and heavy, and it is one of the largest red sandalwood thrones.

title: White Jade Ruyi-Sceptre Carved with an Imperial Poem
description: The white jade Ruyi-Sceptre is masterly carved and polished. It is elegrantly carved on the head with a sinuous dragon in relief, in pursuit of a “flaming pearl”. It symbolizes high rank and power. Above the shaft carved with an imperial poem Yong Baiyu Yunlong Ruyi (“Song on a Cloud and Dragon Ruyi Sceptre”) from Poetry Collection by His Majesty.

title: Imperial White Jade Seal Carved with “Chun Ou Zhai”
description: The jade seal belongs to the category of imperial seals. It has been identified as being in the personal use of the Qianlong Emperor. The white jade used is smooth and glossy. It is a square seal, with a knob featuring a vivid interlaced dragon. The dragon knob is depicted in an eloquent, meticulous, and naturalistic manner. The base is carved with three characters reading “Chun Ou Zhai”. “Chun Ou Zhai”is located to the west of Fengze Garden in the Forbidden City. “Ou” has the meaning of “cultivation”. “Chun Ou Zhai” is the resting place for the emperor during the cultivation ceremony, and it is also the study room for Qianlong in summer.

title: Imperial Chengni-inkstone with Groveling Tiger Decoration and Red Sandalwood Lid Carved with Imperial Poem
description: The vessel is in the shape of a crouching tiger and its colour belongs to the eel yellow among Chengni-inkstones. It is a product recreated by the imperial craftsman who adopted the Jiangzhou Chengni formular. The surface of the inkstone is covered with the mottled green patination and some sprinkling gold. The head of the recumbent tiger is simply carved, with two small sharp ears. It also has two cat-like protruding eyes. The side of the inkstone has some thin edges. The wide edge of the cover can be buckled with the inkstone body. The interior of the cover is carved with an imperial poem referring to the shape of the inkstone.

title: White Jade Carved Figure Story of “The Shepherd Su Wu”
description: The jade use realistic techniques to depict the story of “The Shepherd Su Wu”. After opening the cover, there is a water pot underneath. The layout of the jade is both dense and orderly, dynamic and static, rigid and soft, with outstanding themes and superb craftsmanship.

title: Famille Rose Porcelain Round Brush Holder with an Imperial Poem
medium: Qianlong Reign, Qing Dynasty Hight:9.5cm Qianlong Six-Character Seal Mark and of the Period
description: In the Qianlong period, the writing utensils were not only practical, but also used as a kind of decoration. Therefore, the Qianlong brush holder with imperial poetry were all small in size, and the height was mostly about 10 centimeters. The body of this brush holder is cylindrical and deep, with a flat base. The body is supported on five short feet. The interior and base are enamelled in pale turquoise. The rim and feet are gilt. The outside of the brush holder is decorated with imperial poems, followed by two iron-red seals reading “qianlong chenan” (by the very brush of the Qianlong emperor) and “weiyi jingwei”(be precise, be undivided).

title: Mountain in Spring
medium: Mounted mineral, Ink and colour on silk Dated 1981
description: Zhang Daqian (Chang Dai-Chien，1899-1983), was first named Zhengquan, later renamed Mingyuan, also known by his zi (designated name) Jiyuan and hao (literary name) Daqian, born in NeiJiang, Sichuan. He was renowned for landscape and lotus paintings. Zhang created an immersive breathtaking, and magnificent scenery, which builds a strong visual impact. The unique technique – spilled ink that he invented has impressed the western art field, he was then known as the “Picasso of the East.”

title: Adoring Silence: Flowers, Grass, and Meticulous Insects
medium: Album of thirteen leaves, Ink and colour on paper Dated 1942
description: Qi Baishi (1864-1957), had an original name called Chun Zhi, also known by his zi (designated name) Weiqing and hao (literary name) Lanting. Later changed his name to Minhuang, zi Binsheng, hao Baishi. A native of Xiangtan, Hunan province, one of top 10 calligraphers and artists in the 20th century. Qi is good at painting flower-and-bird, fish-and-insects, scenery, characterized by his vigorous, simple, but creative composition with brief brush strokes, and the richness of his colors. Qi inherited the traditions and characteristics of the literati ink painting. He then enriched and expanded the traditional pantings with his own style.

title: Album of twelve leaves, Ink and colour on paper
medium: Album of twelve leaves, Ink and colour on paper Dated 1946
description: Xu Beihong (1895-1953), originally named Xu Shoukang, was born in Yixing, Jiangsu. Best known for his traditional ink paintings of horses, birds, lions, his art was closely associated with Realism. His art emphasizes the revolution of Chinese art through the incorporation of techniques from the West. He focuses on shape, anatomy, light and shadow. His art accurately depicts human’s bone structures, and presents the spirit of works. He played an important role in Chinese art field during that time.

title: Collective Album of Landscape and Figure
medium: Album of twelve leaves, Ink and colour on silk Dated 1961
description: Lu Yanshao (1909-1993), also called Di, and his zi (designated name) is Wanruo, was born in NanXiang, Shanghai. Lu focused on poem and calligraphy, and was excellent in painting landscape, plum blossoms, bamboo-and-stone. He could make subtle variations through using the water and brush technique skillfully. His landscape is subtle, delicate, tightly structured, and entirely imaginary. He is prominent in landscape painting field.

title: landscape   Album of twelve leaves
medium: Album of twelve leaves, Ink and colour on paper Dated 1953-1954
description: Wu Hufan (1894-1968) had an original name called Yiyan, his zi (designated name) was Yujun, then changed his name to Mingwan, his zi to Dongzhuang. Originally born in Suzhou in the Jiangsu province. He was known for his paintings of bamboo and landscapes. Wu delve into landscape coloring, and his innovative colours brought a sense of modernity into traditional Chinese painting. He was renowned as “Wu in the south and Pu in the north(南吴北溥)” and a member of the “Three Wus and One Feng”, with the other three being Wu Daiqiu, Wu Zishen, and Feng Chaoran.

title: Family of Yang Zhongzi
description: Xu Beihong was born in Jiangsu, China in 1895. He enrolled in the French Department of Aurora University (currently merged with Fudan University) in Shanghai in 1916, working and studying at the same time while also self-studying drawing. In 1917, Xu travelled to Japan to study Western art, returning soon after to become an art instructor at Peking University. He subsequently left for France in 1919, enrolling in the National School of Fine Arts (École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts de Paris) in the following year. In 1927, Xu returned to China, taking on various academic positions: Dean of the Art Department at Nanguo Fine Arts College in Shanghai, Professor of the Art Department at the National Central University (now Nanjing University), and Dean of the Beiping Art College (now Peking University). With the founding of the People’s Republic of China in 1949, Xu served as the Chairman of the Chinese Artists’ Association as well as the President of the Central Academy of Fine Arts. From October 1928 to January 1929, Xu Beihong served as the Dean of Beiping Art College (now Peking University). At the same time, Yang Zhongzi was the Dean of the Music Department. Yang's wife, Yang Yani (Jenny) was a French professor at the public department of the university. In this painting, the Yang family is dressed in Western attire. Their son, Yang Xiaoshi (Chinese, 1923-2017), would later become one of the founders of the English Department at the Shanghai International Studies University.

title: Dance
description: Guan Liang (Chinese, 1900-1986), courtesy name Liang Gong, was born in Panyu, Guangdong. He went to Japan in 1917, studying oil painting at the Kawabata Institution and the Pacific Art Association. After returning to China, he taught at various institutions including the Shanghai Chinese Art College (now Nanjing University of the Arts), Shanghai Arts University, and Hangzhou National College of Art (now China Academy of Art). After the founding of the People’s Republic of China, Guan took on the following rolls: trustee of the Chinese Artists Association, vice chairman of the Shanghai Artists Association, researcher at the Shanghai Research Institute of Culture and History, professional painter at Shanghai Chinese Painting Academy, professor at Zhejiang Academy of Fine Arts (now China Academy of Art), director and advisor of the art research office at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, and committee member of the Shanghai Federation of Literary and Art Circles. Guan Liang developed a signature style of his own that blends Chinese and Western techniques, interpreting the spirit of Chinese art with a modern touch.

title: Snowscape (Luxembourg)
description: Liu Haisu (Chinese, 1896-1994), was born in Changzhou, Jiangsu and was an outstanding fine arts educator, art historian, and painter. In 1912, alongside Wu Shiguang and Zhang Yuguang, he founded the Shanghai Chinese Art College (currently known as the Nanjing University of the Arts), the first school of fine arts in China. In November 1920, Liu also established the first arts magazine in China titled “Art.” From 1929 to 1931, he visited Europe to research Western art, exchanging stories and discussing art with many influential artists including Matisse and Picasso. While in Europe, Liu gave multiple lectures on Chinese art at various universities, further deepening the influence of Chinese culture on Europe. After the founding of the People’s Republic of China, Liu served as the president of East China Arts College and later as its dean when the university relocated to Nanjing and changed its name to the Nanjing University of Arts.

title: Wenfeng Pagoda
description: Pang Xunqin (1906–1985) was of Changshu (Jiangsu Province) descent but was born in Shanghai. From 1921 to 1924, he studied medicine at the Aurora University (now Fudan University). From 1925 to 1930, he studied in France at the Julian Academy (“Académie Julian”) and the Grande Chaumière Academy (“Académie de la Grande Chaumière”). In the following year, having returned to China, he began to teach at Shanghai Changming Art College. In the same year, he founded the Storm Society in Shanghai with Ni Yide, which was the first of its kind that aimed to bring a Western-style art world to China. In the late 1930s, he devoted himself to the collection and arrangement of decorative patterns that originated from China’s previous dynasties in addition to various patterns that belonged to Guizhou minority ethnic groups. He became engaged in the design, teaching, and theoretical research of craftsmanship ever since. He has held academic positions at the Shanghai Academy of Fine Arts (now Nanjing University of the Arts), Central Academy of Art (now China Academy of Art), and Central Academy of Arts and Crafts (now the Academy of Arts and Design at Tsinghua University). His published works include Research of Chinese Decorated Picture of Various Dynasties (“中国历代饰画研究”), On Arts and Crafts (“论工艺美术”), and Designing Arts and Crafts (“工艺美术设计”).

title: Nudes and Masks
description: Pan Yuliang (Chinese, 1895-1977) left for France in 1921 and studied at the Lyon Sino-French Institute (“Institut Franco-Chinois de Lyon”) and the National School of Fine Arts of Lyon (“École Nationale des Beaux-Arts de Lyon”) successively. In 1925, she graduated from the National School of Fine Arts in Paris (“École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts de Paris”) and won the prestigious Rome scholarship to study at the University of Fine Arts in Rome (“Accademia di Belle Arti di Roma). In 1929, she returned to China and served as the president of the Western Painting Department at Shanghai Academy of Fine Arts (now Nanjing University of the Arts) and as a professor at the Art Department of the National Central University (now Nanjing University). She permanently moved to Paris in 1937, where she lived until her death in 1977. Pan blended Chinese and Western painting techniques, using a Chinese brushwork to form the lines of her figures. Starting in the 1940s, she took up painting on rice paper using traditional Chinese brushes and colored inks.

title: Woman in Red
description: Chang Yu (Sanyu) (Chinese, 1901-1966) was born in Sichuan, China. He studied painting at home with his father and later took calligraphy lessons with the renowned Sichuan calligrapher, Zhao Xi (Chinese, 1867-1948). In 1917, he enrolled in the Shanghai Art Academy, then in 1921, he departed for Paris to study art at the Grande Chaumière Academy (Académie de la Grande Chaumière). Chang returned to China briefly before moving to New York. Later in life, he permanently relocated to France and died in Paris in 1966. Influenced by the traditional Chinese painting and calligraphy lessons from his youth, Chang combines Eastern and Western aesthetic modes of expression in his art. He often worked with different materials in the contours of his figures, using Chinese brushes and inks to experiment with distortion and abstraction.

title: 25.06.86(25.06.86 Peach Blossom Land)
description: Zhao Wuji (Zao Wou-Ki) (Chinese-French, 1920-2013) was born in Beijing in 1920. He was admitted to Hangzhou School of Fine Arts in 1935. He went to Paris in 1948 for further artistic studies. He steadily incorporated more Chinese influences in his work, fusing Eastern and Western aesthetics. In 1971 he rediscovered the challenging technique of China ink. He was appointed teacher of mural painting at the École Nationale Supérieure des Arts Décoratifs in 1980. He was invited to teach painting and charcoal drawing at Hangzhou School of Fine Arts. He decided to stop working with oil paints in 2008. He settled in Dully, Switzerland. The painting 25.06.86 Peach Blossom Land was completed in 1986, at a time when Zao’s life and international reputation were at zenith. The work not only showcases the artist’s creative success and freedom, it also reflects the vast sweep and laid back nature of his emotional world.

title: Red Stone
description: Zhou Chunya was born in Chongqing, China in 1955; he currently lives and works in Shanghai and Chengdu. Zhou graduated from the Sichuan Fine Arts Institute in 1982 after studying printmaking. He then continued his education at the School of Arts of the University of Kassel (“Kunsthochschule Kassel”) in Germany, finishing his studies in 1988. As one of the leading figures in the Chinese contemporary art world, Zhou excels in his masterful use of colors. In over four decades of artistic creation, he has persistently challenged himself in the field of oil painting, drawing, and sculpture, constantly seeking new ways of innovation and transformation. In his “Stone Series” from the early 1990s, Zhou combines the colors of Neo-Expressionism with elements of “mountains and stone,” a traditional subject matter in Chinese literati paintings, consequently arriving at his own personal style. Around 2005, Zhou began working on his most celebrated work, the “Peach Blossom Series,” which visually articulates the artist’s renewed spirit and enthusiasm towards both art and life. Zhou’s recent artworks are a testament to his constant research and profound understanding of Chinese traditional culture.

title: Two Jin of Beef
description: Zhang Enli was born in Jilin Province in 1965. He graduated from the Arts & Design Institute of Wuxi Technical University (now a part of Jiangnan University) in 1989 and taught at the Arts and Design Institute of Donghua University afterwards. He currently lives and works in Shanghai. Zhang Enli’s œuvre can be roughly divided into three categories: figurative paintings from the 1990s that focus on ordinary people and their lives, still-life paintings after the 2000s depicting various “containers” that trace the passage of time, and, more recently, abstract paintings that record memory and explore the subconscious. Since 2007, his “Space Painting” series mobilizes the viewer’s bodily experience amidst a symphony of time and space, thus stimulating new possibilities in one of the world’s oldest mediums, pulling oil painting towards a new direction.

title: Appearance of Crosses 2015-4
description: Ding Yi was born in 1962 in Shanghai, where he currently lives and works. He first graduated from the Shanghai Art and Design Academy in 1983, then from the Shanghai Academy of Fine Arts, Shanghai University in 1990. Ding’s practice encompasses painting, sculpture, spatial installation, and architecture. Beginning in the late 1980s, Ding started working primarily with the symbol “+” and its variant “x” as an expression of structure and rationality, reflecting the innate essence of all things through this pictorial imagery.

title: Reclining Nude with Toile de Jouy（Nu allongé à la toile de Jouy）
description: Foujita Tsuguharu (Léonard Tsuguharu Foujita) (Japanese-French, 1886-1968) was born in Tokyo, Japan. Following the advice of Mori Ōgai, who was the superior of Foujita’s father’s at work, Foujita enrolled in the Tokyo School of Fine Arts (now Tokyo University of the Arts) for his education. Later, he left for France in 1913 to continue his studies. He was a member of the School of Paris and is known for his portraits, nudes, and paintings of cats. Fujita applied traditional Japanese ink and wash techniques to Western paintings, presenting a rich show of expression. In Reclining Nude with Toile de Jouy (“Nu allongé à la toile de Jouy”) (1949), the simplicity of the contours and colors renders the nude immediately lifelike. The fabric of "Toile de Jouy" takes its name from a celebrated textile factory at Jouy-en-Josas (a village near Versailles). The linen fabric is decorated with designs of landscapes and figures, standing in stark contrast with the sitter’s alabaster skin and the black background behind.

title: Autumn
description: Kazuo Shiraga was born in Hyogo, Japan in 1924 and graduated from the Kyoto Municipal Special School of Painting in 1948. He once acted as a part of “zero society” before joining the Gutai Group, consequently becoming one of the leading members in the movement. His gestural style was influenced by American Abstract Expressionism and is indicative of his participation in the avant-garde Gutai Group. Shiraga developed a format that combined painting with performance and used his own body as a physical means towards artistic creation. He also acquired a Buddhist priesthood at Enryakuji-Temple in Mount Hiei (where he received his Buddhist name, Sodo Shiraga). In Autumn, Shiraga’s bodily movements leave a thick trail of paint on the canvas, creating a work that is both dynamic and full of energy.

title: Nu couché (Reclining Nude)
description: Amedeo Modigliani (Italian, 1884-1920) was an Italian Jewish painter and sculptor who worked mainly in France. He is known for portraits and nudes in a modern style characterized by a surreal elongation of faces, necks, and figures.He started by studying painting but was introduced to sculpture upon meeting Constantin Brancusi in Paris in 1909. From 1909 to 1914, he devoted himself mainly to sculpture. Modigliani returned entirely to painting with new eyes in 1915, working in the linear style that he is so well known for today. He died of tubercular meningitis, at the age of 35, in Paris.

title: No. 36 (Black Stripe)
description: Mark Rothko (American (born Russia, now Latvia), 1903-1970) As a self-taught artist, Rothko worked in a realistic style before arriving at his distinctive color field paintings in 1949. He is associated with the Abstract Expressionist School in New York, but unlike his contemporaries, his paintings are gesture-less and composed of large floating blocks of pure color.

title: Le toit du monde (The Roof of the World)
description: René Magritte (Belgian, 1898-1967) is one of the most well-known Surrealist painters and his work is immediately recognizable for its portrayal of clouds, green apples, and bowler hats. Constructing his paintings around traps and uncertainties, Magritte pursued a signature figurative style that combined mystery with comedy.

title: Pumpkin
artist: 草間 彌生 Yayoi Kusama
description: Yayoi Kusama was born in 1929 in Nagano, Japan. After a stint studying traditional Japanese painting in Kyoto, Kusama left school and moved to New York in 1958. By the 1960s, the prolific artist was producing paintings, drawings, sculpture, Happenings, installation, fashion, and film. In 1973, Kusama returned to Japan. She continues to produce paintings and sculpture, and poetry and fiction from the 1980s. Converting her own illusion to artistic creation, Yayoi Kusama uses a lot of dotted patterns with strong color contrasts in her works, which are extending from canvas to articles, furniture, body, and even space. It is these dots that she thinks form an infinitely huge net which embodies the constant reproduction and multiplying of her life.

title: Girl with a Long Fuse
description: 奈良 美智 Nara Yoshitomo (Japanese, b.1959)was born in 1959 in Aomori of Japan. Earning both his BFA and MFA from the Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music, and later studying at the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf during the late 1980s. He lived and studied in Germany from 1988 to 2000.His early works were influenced by european 20th Century Expressionism. Around 2001, Nara became associated with an avant-garde group of Japanese artists known as Superflat. His most well-known and repeated subject is a young child with piercing eyes. Nara dedicated a poem: It looks like walking on top of a string It is me riding on a boat, alone It is empty and quiet above and below me In that, I slowly move forward Swimming forward at the same time My hand will probably reach somewhere I don't know if that's true but I keep going forward - Yoshitomo Nara

title: From Line 780271
medium: Mineral pigment and glue on canvas
description: Lee Ufan (Korean, b. 1936) Lee Ufan was born in Haman County, South Korea in 1936. He attended the College of Fine Arts at Seoul National University before emigrating to Japan in 1956. There, he obtained a degree in philosophy at Tokyo’s Nihon University in 1961. Lee is best known as one of the leading members of the Mono-ha movement. He is also a representative member of Dansaekhwa (“monochrome painting”). Lee divides his time between Japan and France.

title: And then 1000 (A Deep Ocean of Ultramarine)
description: Takashi Murakami was born in 1962 in Tokyo, Japan. His style is characterized by a synthesis of pop culture and fine art. In particular, Murakami is known for his graphic and colorful cartoon style that is inspired by Japanese anime and manga. Murakami's work includes paintings, sculptures, drawings, animations, and collaborations with world famous brands. He coined the term “superflat,” which describes traditional Japanese aesthetics and serves as the artist’s commentary on postwar Japanese culture and society.

title: Ecriture NO. 9-74
description: Park Seo-Bo (Korean, b. 1931) Park Seo-Bo was born in South Korea in 1931. He graduated with a B.A in painting from Hong-Ik University in Seoul in 1954. After becoming the dean of the College of Fine Arts there in 1973, he was further awarded an Honorary Doctorate Degree in 2000. Park is regarded as a leading figure in contemporary Korean art and is a recipient of the Korean Silver Crown Cultural Medal in 2011 as well as the Asia Arts Game Changer Award in 2018. He is also credited as being the father of the Dansaekhwa (“monochrome painting”) movement. Park’s renowned “Ecriture” series first began in the late 1960s. As a series of paintings, they are intricately linked to notions of time, space, and material.

title: The Big Picture
medium: Pigment and pencil on black Aquacryl on canvas and aluminium
description: Shirazeh Houshiary was born in Shiraz, Iran in 1955. She left for London in 1974 and studied at the Chelsea School of Art (currently Chelsea College of Art and Design). She first garnered international attention in the 1980s through her sculptural work, which earned her a Turner Prize nomination in 1994. Since then, her practice has swelled to encompass paintings, installation works, architectural projects, and film. She lives and works in London.

title: A Picture of a Lion
description: David Hockney was born in Bradford, England in 1937. He is a painter, draftsman, printmaker, stage designer, and photographer. After graduating from the Bradford School of Art in 1957, he continued his studies at the Royal College of Art in London from 1959 to 1962. Hockney was an important contributor to the British pop art movement in the 1960s with the swimming pools in Los Angeles serving as one of his favorite subjects. Outside of painting, he has also worked extensively with photography. In the 1990s, he used fax machines and laser printers as an artistic means of creation. In 2009, Hockney also began experimenting with the Brushes app to create paintings on iPhones and iPads.

title: Elements III
description: Brice Marden is an American artist. Born in 1938 in New York, He received his BFA from Boston University in 1961 and his MFA from Yale University’s School of Art and Architecture in 1963. Contributing to the emerging aesthetic of Minimalism, Marden made his first monochromatic paintings in 1964. His later works are visually different to his previous monochromatic works. Combining the Abstract Expressionism with the Minimalism, Marden achieved a balance between emotional intensity and formal simplicity. Conjuring ancient architecture and American modernism, the spiritual and material, Elements III is part of Brice Marden’s celebrated eponymous series created between 1981 and 1984.
